title: Grounds on Which Money is Stopped on a Keyturn Host Payout Account
content:
Money is stopped from leaving a Keyturn Host Payout Account for a stated ground and never without one, the grounds being an open claim, an unfinished deposit check, a disputed chargeback, missing tax documentation and a risk review.

| Ground | Notice before the hold takes effect |
|---|---|
| An open claim | The schedule's notice period |
| An unfinished deposit check | The schedule's notice period |
| A disputed chargeback | The schedule's notice period |
| Missing tax documentation | The schedule's notice period |
| A risk review | None; the hold takes effect at once and the host is told afterwards |

The host is told the schedule's notice period before a hold takes effect, except where the ground is a risk review, in which case the hold takes effect at once and the host is told afterwards, because notice would defeat the purpose of the review.

## Review and release

A hold is looked at within the schedule's review period in business days counted from the day it was placed, and a hold whose ground has fallen away is released rather than left standing.

## What a hold does and does not stop

A hold stops money leaving but never stops money arriving, so earnings continue to post to a held account and the host can see what is accruing.

## When a hold becomes a suspension

Where a hold turns out to rest on something more serious the account is suspended instead, and a suspended account settles nothing in either direction until the decision is taken.

## One ground at a time

Only one ground stands on the account at a time; where a second ground arises the more serious of the two is recorded, and the host is told which one is now blocking the money.

The ground is a matter of the account's own record: the state the account stands in, the ground recorded against it and the account's own reference number, read before the hold is placed. An account on which a hold may be placed stands either active or on hold.

## Points of judgement

**A host on hold asks whether their earnings have stopped.** Earnings continue to post; it is money leaving that is stopped.

**A second ground arises while a hold already stands.** The more serious of the two is the one recorded, and the host is told which one is now blocking the money.
